title: Best One-Click and Easy Apply Job Apps in 2026, Compared and Ranked
summary: Easy Apply helps, but only on one site. Tsenta ranks 2026's one-click job apps, from LinkedIn and Indeed to agents that apply across 30+ ATSes for you.
body_markdown:
*Published on October 30, 2026 by Tsenta*


Tsenta is the best one-click job application app in 2026 for jobs that send you to the employer's own application system, and LinkedIn Easy Apply and Indeed Apply are the best free one-click options for jobs that stay on the job board. One click only works on the site that hosts the form. When a listing sends you to the employer's system,[Tsenta](https://tsenta.com/) keeps going and submits there, on 30+ ATSes including Workday.


We compared seven options: Tsenta, LinkedIn Easy Apply (including the LinkedIn mobile app), Indeed Apply, Simplify, Jobright, LazyApply and Scale.jobs. Every competitor price, cap and feature below was checked on that company's own site, help center or app store listing on October 30, 2026.


## What Is a One-Click Job Application App?


A one-click job application app lets you send an application with one tap or click, using a profile and résumé you saved once. The category splits three ways:


- **On-platform one-click apply.** LinkedIn Easy Apply and Indeed Apply submit a short form hosted on the job site itself. They're free, fast, and work only on listings where the employer turned them on.
- **Browser extensions.** Simplify Copilot, Jobright's extension and LazyApply fill application forms on other sites. Some only fill fields and leave the submit to you; some submit.
- **Agents and services.** Tsenta, Simplify Autopilot, Jobright Agent and Scale.jobs take the application off your hands. Tsenta's agent applies on the employer's own system from its cloud. Scale.jobs uses human assistants.


## Where One-Click Apply Stops, and Where an Agent Keeps Going


One-click apply breaks at the redirect. LinkedIn's help center says that, depending on the employer's settings, you'll see an Easy Apply or an Apply button, and an Apply button routes you "to that company's website or job board to continue the application process." Indeed works the same way: jobs without its Easily apply label direct you to the employer's website, and Indeed's own app guide warns that "these applications may not always be mobile-friendly."


On the other side of that redirect is the employer's applicant tracking system (ATS): Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, iCIMS and dozens more. That usually means creating an account, re-entering your work history, uploading your résumé again, and answering screening questions, often on a form that wasn't built for a phone.


That's where an agent earns its place. When you pick a role in Tsenta, the agent handles the login or sign-up, fills every field, drafts the open-ended answers in your voice, uploads your documents and submits, then routes the recruiter's reply back to that application. It runs in Tsenta's cloud, so your phone can be locked and your laptop closed.


## What to Look for in a One-Click Job Application App


- **How far one tap gets you.** Does the app submit, or does it fill fields and wait for you?
- **Coverage past the job board.** Does it work when a listing sends you to Workday, Greenhouse or Lever?
- **Mobile usability.** Can you apply from your phone, and does the work happen somewhere other than your phone?
- **Price per submitted application.** Are plans and caps published?
- **Control.** Can you review what goes out, and is your account safe using it?

## Best One-Click and Easy Apply Job Apps in 2026


### 1. Tsenta


Tsenta is an AI job application agent backed by Y Combinator (S26). It watches 50,000+ company career pages, matches roles to your résumé, tailors your résumé for each role, and applies on the employer's own system across 30+ ATSes, including Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, iCIMS, SmartRecruiters and Oracle Cloud ([full list](https://tsenta.com/ai-disclosure) ). One tap starts the application; the agent does the rest.


**What one tap does:** swipe right on a match in the app, reply yes to a text, or pick a role on the web. The agent logs in or signs up, fills every field, drafts open-ended answers, uploads documents, submits, and tracks the reply.


**Where it stops:** an employer system Tsenta doesn't support yet, or a missing answer or verification step it needs you for. Tsenta also doesn't submit LinkedIn Easy Apply, so use LinkedIn for those listings.


**Mobile usability:** native[iOS and Android apps](https://tsenta.com/mobile) where you browse roles matched to your résumé, swipe to apply, review changes and track each submission. You can also text Tsenta over[iMessage or WhatsApp](https://tsenta.com/messaging) and reply yes to apply. The application runs in Tsenta's cloud either way, so nothing has to stay open on your phone.

Only successful submissions count. Quarterly and annual billing lower the effective monthly rate by up to 36%. See[Tsenta pricing](https://tsenta.com/pricing) .


**Pros:**


- Keeps going past the redirect, on 30+ employer systems including Workday
- Résumé tailored per role, plus a cover letter where the employer accepts one; with résumé review on, changes show as a diff you approve or edit
- Tracker included on every tier, with recruiter replies routed to the right application

- No LinkedIn Easy Apply submissions

**Best for:** anyone whose target employers post on their own career sites and ATSes, and anyone who wants to apply from a phone without filling ATS forms on it.


### 2. LinkedIn Easy Apply (including the LinkedIn mobile app)


LinkedIn Easy Apply is the most familiar one-click apply. On a listing that offers it, you click or tap Easy Apply, fill in the popup screens, review, and submit, using your LinkedIn profile and résumé. LinkedIn says you can use it from a desktop browser or the LinkedIn mobile app.


**What one tap does:** opens a short LinkedIn-hosted form prefilled from your profile. You confirm and submit.


**Where it stops:** "Depending on the employer's settings, you'll see an Easy Apply or Apply button," per LinkedIn. Apply routes you to the company's site. LinkedIn also has daily and speed limits on Easy Apply, resets the daily count at the end of the day (UTC), and says it may lower a member's limit if activity looks inauthentic. You can't edit or withdraw an application once it's submitted.


**Mobile usability:** strong. The LinkedIn app on iOS and Android supports Easy Apply end to end.


**Pricing:** free with a LinkedIn account.


**Pros:**


- Free, official, and as fast as one-click gets
- Works the same in the mobile app as on desktop
- No third-party tool touching your account


**Cons:**


- Only works on listings where the employer turned it on
- A capped number of applications per day
- No per-role résumé tailoring unless you do it yourself


**Best for:** listings that show the Easy Apply button. For the ones that don't, see Tsenta above.


### 3. Indeed Apply (Indeed Quick Apply)


Indeed Apply is Indeed's one-click option, which Indeed says is "also known as Indeed Easy Apply or Indeed Quick Apply." Listings that support it show an Easily apply badge, and you apply on Indeed with your Indeed profile and résumé instead of being sent to a career site.


**What one tap does:** opens an application on Indeed with your saved résumé attached. You answer the employer's questions and submit, and you can save a draft. Applications show up in the Applied tab of My jobs.


**Where it stops:** jobs without Easily apply direct you to the employer's website, and Indeed says those "may not always be mobile-friendly, so you may choose to apply later from a computer."


**Mobile usability:** good for Easily apply listings in the Indeed app. Off-site applications are where it gets slow.


**Pricing:** free.


**Pros:**


- Free and built into the Indeed app
- Default for jobs employers post directly on Indeed
- Drafts and an Applied tab to track what you sent


**Cons:**


- Only on listings with the Easily apply badge
- Off-site applications may not be mobile-friendly, per Indeed
- No per-role résumé tailoring unless you do it yourself


**Best for:** Indeed-heavy searches, on listings that carry the Easily apply badge.


### 4. Simplify


Simplify has two different things under one name. Simplify Copilot is a free browser extension that, per Simplify, "autofills job applications on 100,000+ company career sites in one click." You still review and submit. Autopilot, part of the paid Simplify+ plan, "fills and submits after you choose the job and preparation options, without a review step," on supported postings. Simplify doesn't publish the list of systems Autopilot supports.


**What one tap does:** with Copilot, fills the fields on the page you're on. With Autopilot, submits the application, with your résumé tailored to the role.


**Where it stops:** Autopilot works only on supported postings, and Simplify+ includes 20 credits a week, with one used per successful submission. Unused credits don't roll over.


**Mobile usability:** Simplify has an iOS app where you can find jobs, hand them to Autopilot and track them. Simplify's help center mentions the iOS app, not an Android one.


**Pricing:** Copilot autofill, the résumé builder and job tracker are free. Simplify+ is $19.99 a week, $39.99 a month or $89.99 for three months on the web, per Simplify's help center; App Store pricing can differ.


**Pros:**


- Very good free autofill extension
- Autopilot submits on supported postings
- iOS app


**Cons:**


- 20 Autopilot submissions a week on Simplify+
- No review step on Autopilot; use Copilot if you want to check first
- No published list of Autopilot-supported systems


**Best for:** people who want free autofill on their laptop and a modest number of hands-off submissions a week. More in[Tsenta vs Simplify](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-simplify) .


### 5. Jobright


Jobright is an AI job search copilot focused on matching. Its site promises "1-Click Application Autofill," and its extension autofills on supported application sites. Jobright Agent, launched in 2025, is described by Jobright as able to tailor, fill and apply for you, with access "subject to plan and availability."


**What one tap does:** the extension fills supported forms for you to submit. Agent applies where your plan includes it.


**Where it stops:** Agent access varies by plan, and Jobright lists U.S.-based roles only.


**Mobile usability:** Jobright has iOS and Android apps for matches, alerts and tracking. The App Store description doesn't describe applying inside the app, so expect to finish applications on a computer.


**Pricing:** there's a free plan. Jobright says to "review current features, credits, and pricing in your account," and it has no public job-seeker pricing page.


**Pros:**


- Strong job matching and a well-rated iOS app
- Free plan for matching and tracking
- Autofill extension for supported sites


**Cons:**


- Paid pricing isn't public
- U.S. roles only
- The phone app is for finding and tracking more than applying


**Best for:** U.S. job seekers who want help finding roles and are fine applying from a laptop. More in[Tsenta vs Jobright](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-jobright) .


### 6. Scale.jobs


Scale.jobs isn't one-click software. It's a service where human assistants apply for you. Its pricing page says assistants can "apply anywhere you can: any ATS, any portal, any form," with a tailored résumé, a cover letter and a proof screenshot for each application.


**What one tap does:** approves roles for your assistant to apply to.


**Where it stops:** speed and cost. Scale.jobs says assistants apply within 24 hours, which is quick for people but slower than software, and the price per application is higher.


**Mobile usability:** Scale.jobs has iOS and Android "Job Concierge" apps for tracking applications, approving roles and messaging your team.


**Pricing:** one-time packages: Standard $399 for 500 applications, Accelerator $599 for 1,000, Ultimate $999 for 1,500.


**Pros:**


- A person handles the portal, and Scale.jobs says that covers any ATS or form
- Tailored documents and proof for each application
- No subscription


**Cons:**


- $0.40 to $0.80 per application, against about 3 cents on Tsenta Starter
- Slower than software, with a turnaround of up to a day
- A team of people works with your personal details


**Best for:** people who want a human in the loop and are willing to pay for it. More in[Tsenta vs Scale.jobs](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-scale-jobs) .


### 7. LazyApply


LazyApply is a Chrome extension that uses what it calls Job GPT to fill applications and apply in bulk. Its homepage says it applies on "platforms like Greenhouse, Dice, Indeed and Ziprecruiter."


**What one tap does:** starts a bulk run from the extension on the job boards it supports.


**Where it stops:** daily caps by plan, and coverage limited to the platforms it names.


**Mobile usability:** none. LazyApply doesn't mention a mobile app, so it's a desktop Chrome workflow.


**Pricing:** annual plans only. Basic is $99 a year for 15 applications a day with one résumé profile, Premium is $149 a year for 150 a day with five, and Ultimate is $999 a year for 1,500 a day with 20. Each plan requires a Gmail address, and there's a 30-day money-back guarantee.


**Pros:**


- High daily caps on the top plans
- Simple to start from Chrome
- Money-back window


**Cons:**


- No monthly plan and no free tier
- No mobile app
- Coverage tied to the job boards it names


**Best for:** desktop users who want bulk applying on the boards LazyApply supports. More in[Tsenta vs LazyApply](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-lazyapply) .


## How People Combine One-Click Apply With an Agent


You don't have to pick one. A practical setup:


1. **Use Easy Apply and Indeed Apply where the badge shows.** They're free and fast, and nothing beats them on their own listings.
2. **Hand off every "Apply on company site" job to an agent.** That's where Tsenta does its work: the Workday, Greenhouse and Lever forms one-click can't reach.
3. **Let the agent find roles too.** Tsenta watches 50,000+ company career pages, so roles can surface before LinkedIn or Indeed index them.
4. **Apply from your phone, not on it.** Swipe in the Tsenta app or reply yes over iMessage or WhatsApp, and let the cloud do the form.
5. **Keep one tracker.** Tsenta routes recruiter replies to the right application, so you're not matching emails to a spreadsheet.


International students can add a step: Tsenta surfaces the sponsorship signals it knows about for a role or company and uses your work authorization when answering application questions. It can't promise any employer will sponsor. See[Tsenta for international students](https://tsenta.com/international) .

## FAQs About One-Click and Easy Apply Job Apps in 2026


### What is the difference between one-click apply and an AI job application agent?


One-click apply, like LinkedIn Easy Apply or Indeed Apply, submits a form hosted on that job site using your saved profile and résumé, and only on listings where the employer turned it on. An AI job application agent such as Tsenta goes to the employer's own application system, handles the login, fills every field, drafts open-ended answers, uploads documents and submits. Tsenta does this on 30+ ATSes, including Workday.


### Why does LinkedIn Easy Apply stop working for some jobs?


Easy Apply depends on the employer's settings. LinkedIn's help center says that when a listing shows Apply instead of Easy Apply, you're routed to the company's website or job board to continue. That is usually an ATS like Workday or Greenhouse, where you create an account and fill in the form again. Tsenta applies on those employer systems for you.


### Can you use LinkedIn Easy Apply on the LinkedIn mobile app?


Yes. LinkedIn says you can use Easy Apply from a desktop browser or the LinkedIn mobile app on iOS and Android. You tap Easy Apply, fill in the screens, review, and tap Submit. You can't edit or withdraw an application after it's submitted, and jobs without Easy Apply send you to the employer's site.


### Is there a daily limit on LinkedIn Easy Apply?


Yes. LinkedIn sets daily and speed limits on Easy Apply submissions. The daily limit resets at the end of the day (UTC), applying rapidly triggers a temporary pause, and LinkedIn says it may lower a member's limit if activity looks inauthentic. LinkedIn doesn't publish the exact number.


### What is Indeed Quick Apply?


Indeed Quick Apply is another name for Indeed Apply, which Indeed also calls Indeed Easy Apply. Listings that support it show an Easily apply badge, and you apply on Indeed with your Indeed profile and résumé, including in the Indeed app. Jobs without it send you to the employer's website, which Indeed says may not always be mobile-friendly.


### What is the best mobile app to apply for jobs quickly in 2026?


For listings that support it, the LinkedIn and Indeed apps are the fastest free way to apply from your phone. For jobs that send you to an employer's system, Tsenta's iOS and Android apps let you swipe to apply while the agent completes the application in its cloud, and you can also reply yes over iMessage or WhatsApp. Simplify's iOS app can submit through Autopilot on supported postings with Simplify+.


### Does Simplify apply for you?


It depends on the feature. Simplify Copilot, the free Chrome extension, autofills supported fields and you review and submit yourself. Autopilot, part of Simplify+ ($39.99 a month on the web), fills and submits on supported postings without a review step, and each successful submission uses one of 20 weekly credits. Tsenta submits on 30+ ATSes, with plans from $19 for 600 applications.


### How do I apply to Workday jobs from my phone?


A Workday application usually means creating an account and working through several pages, which is slow on a phone, and Indeed notes that applications on employer websites may not be mobile-friendly. With Tsenta, you swipe to apply in the iOS or Android app and the agent handles the Workday sign-in, the form, the documents and the submit from its cloud. More in[the best AI agents for Workday](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-ai-agents-workday-ats-portals) .


### Can Tsenta apply while my phone is locked?


Yes. Tsenta's applications run in its cloud, so you can close the app and come back later to see progress, any question that needs your answer, recruiter replies and completed submissions. You pick the roles by default. Auto Apply, which picks and submits matches on its own, is on the Power plan.


### How much does Tsenta cost compared with LazyApply, Simplify and Scale.jobs?


Tsenta's first 25 applications are free with no card. Then Starter is $19 for 600 applications, Pro is $39 for 1,500 and Power is $99 for 4,500 per 30-day cycle. LazyApply is $99, $149 or $999 a year with daily caps of 15, 150 or 1,500. Simplify+ is $39.99 a month with 20 Autopilot submissions a week. Scale.jobs charges $399 to $999 one time for 500 to 1,500 applications submitted by people.


### What is Tsenta's free plan?


Your first 25 applications are free with no credit card. Those 25 run the full agent: matching, a résumé tailored to each role plus a cover letter where the employer accepts one, submission on the employer's system, and tracking. Only successful submissions count. After that you can move to Starter, Pro or Power.
